final_rationale: The verdict changes only because the Actor narrowed the claim to a policy-bounded position already reachable from the admissible record, not because any new admissible evidence was introduced. The record still shows an unresolved weakness in a named launch use case, no approved mitigation, and a conflicting model-card draft; under the policy text, that defeats clean certification. But the same record also supports the narrower conclusion that certification can be compliant only on a caveated basis tied to explicit disclosure of the limitation. That distinction matters: caveated compliance is supportable as a constrained governance position, while clean certification remains unsupported on this record.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the model card or release record has actually been updated to disclose the student-aid limitation.
The draft runbook remains unapproved and still lacks the required owner and alert threshold, so it cannot satisfy the clean-certification predicate.
The underlying packet still contains a conflicting 'no known material limitations' statement, which must not be relied on.
Compliance here is only for the narrowed position: certification is supportable only if explicitly conditioned on disclosure of the unresolved limitation, not as a clean certification.
